Subject: Intermittent egress drops for large MTU transfers from private deployment

Hi Michael / Neha,

We're seeing intermittent failures when transferring large files from our on-prem cluster to S3 via the private deployment connection. Transfers that use larger segment sizes (MTU ~9000 on our side) occasionally stall and then time out. I attached a tcpdump (pcap) showing repeated retransmits and some "ICMP Fragmentation Needed" messages followed by silent drops.

Details:
- Affected system: app1.clearstone.local (10.23.14.21)
- Destination: s3 proxy through Redwood private edge (customer VPC)
- First seen: 2025-07-09 08:55 PDT
- We observe DF bit set and no successful fragmentation path; occasional SYN retries and then connection reset.

We've pulled a pcap and a route table screenshot (attached) and opened an incident: SUP-7891. Can you advise whether there are MTU assumptions or NAT/ACL behavior on Redwood's private edge that could drop fragments or block ICMP path MTU responses? This is impacting nightly backups.

Attached: clearstone_capture_20250709.pcap.tgz, clearstone-routes.png

Thanks,
Sam Walker
Network Engineer, Clearstone Health
netops@clearstone.com

Subject: Re: Intermittent egress drops for large MTU transfers from private deployment

Thanks Sam — appreciate the quick capture. I've looped in Neha (network team) and asked our on-call infra engineers to take a look. Initial asks:

1) Can you confirm whether the TCP stack on app1 is using TSO/GSO (common for 9000 MTU setups)? If so, please temporarily disable TSO/GSO for a quick test.
2) Can you run an iperf3 test from app1 to a small reachable host behind our private edge with -M 9000 and attach the output?
3) Any firewall or NAT device configuration between app1 and the Clearstone edge? If there's a third-party firewall doing MSS clamping it would help to know the model and config.

From our side we'll:
- Check SNAT behavior on the private edge (whether fragments with DF are being dropped).
- Inspect ACL/security group counters for denied ICMP types and ephemeral port exhaustion.
- Review the pcap for ICMP "Fragmentation Needed" responses and whether they reach the origin.

I've attached our egress troubleshooting playbook (redwood-egress-playbook-v2.pdf) with steps we'll run. We'll aim to have a short remediation plan after the first round of info.

—Michael

Subject: Re: Intermittent egress drops for large MTU transfers from private deployment

Adding our triage notes (quick summary) after an initial pass on the pcap Sam attached. Quoted below is Sam's original report.

Quick findings:
- The pcap clearly shows TCP segments leaving app1 with DF set and 9000-ish payload sizes (TSO likely). We see ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) from a mid-path device but those ICMP replies are not consistently reaching the origin — looks like they're being dropped or rate-limited somewhere.
- The private edge SNAT device appears to perform a re-write and then apply an egress ACL; fragments (or the responses about fragmentation) are being discarded when the DF bit prevents fragmentation at the edge.
- Security group / ACL counters show denied traffic for ICMP type 3 on the egress path (policy denies non-essential ICMP in some customer templates).

Hypothesis: combination of (a) TSO/GSO on the host producing large frames with DF, (b) intermediate device or ACL dropping ICMP "Fragmentation Needed", and (c) SNAT/edge path not performing transparent MSS clamping — result: PMTU blackhole.

Immediate mitigation options (choose 1, fastest to test):
- Enable MSS clamping on the Clearstone edge firewall (clamp to 1400-1452). This is quick and non-disruptive.
- Temporarily disable TSO/GSO on app1 (ethtool) to force host segmentation; will avoid large DF packets.
- Allow ICMP type 3 code 4 through egress ACLs so PMTU discovery can succeed.

Suggested remediation plan:
1) Clearstone to enable MSS clamping (400-600 seconds test window) — least risky.
2) If unsuccessful, disable TSO/GSO on a test host and re-run iperf.
3) If packet drops persist, we'll schedule a short maintenance window to capture full path tcpdumps and apply an ACL rule update on the private edge to permit ICMP PMTU queries.

I've attached the playbook steps and a small snippet of the route table for context. Also filing internal Jira SUP-7891 to track.

Next steps for Clearstone: can you enable MSS clamping and re-run the nightly backup for one job and upload the new capture? We'll monitor rate and success.

Neha Kapoor
Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@clearstone.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress drops for large MTU transfers from private deployment

Thanks Neha — we enabled MSS clamping on the Clearstone edge firewall (clamped to 1440) and toggled off TSO on the test host. We re-ran the backup job and it completed end-to-end without retransmits. We also confirmed ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages are now visible back to the origin when we briefly re-enabled them for the test.

We're going to roll the MSS clamp change to the rest of the cluster tonight during the maintenance window and will monitor. If we still see issues we'll reopen SUP-7891 with the additional captures. Appreciate the quick turnaround and the remediation playbook.

Sam Walker
Network Engineer, Clearstone Health
